verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is a 10-day crewed test flight.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '10-day mission'; R2: 'approximately 10-day Artemis II mission'; R3: 'Duration: 10 days'; R5: '9 days, 1 hour, 32 minutes'; R7: 'approximately 10-day mission'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm ~10-day crewed test flight duration.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission will follow a "figure-eight" trajectory.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'fly two orbits around Earth before heading to the moon in a figure-eight pattern'; R6: 'venture around the Moon in a figure-eight pattern'

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission will send four astronauts around the Moon and back.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'lifting four astronauts toward space... around the moon but not land there'; R3: 'carrying four astronauts on a journey around the Moon'; R5: 'Crewed lunar flyby mission'
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm four astronauts on lunar flyby and return.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission will cover about 230,000 miles.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'round trip of more than 695,000 miles'; R5: 'Distance travelled 700,237 mi'
verifications.reasoning: References state total distance ~700,000 miles, directly contradicting 230,000 miles.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission will launch from Kennedy Space Center.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Kennedy Space Center in Florida'; R3: 'Kennedy Space Center in Florida'

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission will launch on the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA rocket... Space Launch System'; R2: 'SLS (Space Launch System) rocket'

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft will perform two high Earth orbits for system checks.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'fly two orbits of Earth'; R1: 'high-Earth orbit... swung out more than 43,000 miles... check important systems'; R5: 'highly elliptical, high Earth orbit... system checkouts'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm high Earth orbits (period ~24h implying ~2 orbits) for checkouts.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft will execute a translunar injection (TLI) burn to travel to the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Orion will fire its engines to push it on a path toward the moon'; R7: 'TRANS-LUNAR INJECTION (TLI)'

verifications.claim: The SLS rocket will lift off from Pad 39B.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Kennedy Space Center’s Launch Complex 39B'; R7: 'pad 39B'

verifications.claim: The SLS rocket will insert Orion into a high elliptical orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'highly elliptical orbit'; R1: 'large looping orbit that swung out more than 43,000 miles'
verifications.reasoning: SLS upper stage places Orion in high elliptical Earth orbit.

verifications.claim: The high elliptical orbit involves a perigee raising maneuver.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'PRM (perigee raise maneuver)'; R7: 'PERIGEE RAISE MANEUVER (PRM) BURN'

verifications.claim: The high elliptical orbit is for initial checkouts.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'provides time to check important systems aboard Orion'; R3: 'verify that all systems are performing as expected'
verifications.reasoning: Purpose clearly stated as system checkouts.

verifications.claim: The crew will perform a manual handling exercise.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Mr. Glover manually flew the spacecraft'; R3: 'astronauts will also take manual control... proximity operations demonstration'

verifications.claim: The crew will separate from the Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (ICPS).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The Orion spacecraft separated from the upper stage'; R7: 'CREW MODULE SEPARATION FROM SERVICE MODULE INTERIM CRYOGENIC PROPULSION STAGE (ICPS)'

verifications.claim: Crew separation from the Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (ICPS) is to test maneuvering capabilities.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'mimicked the maneuvers that will be used... for docking'; R2: 'proximity operations demonstration... manually maneuver Orion'

verifications.claim: Orion's main engine will fire for translunar injection (TLI).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'trans-lunar injection (TLI) burn using the ESM's AJ10 main engine'; R7: 'TRANS-LUNAR INJECTION (TLI) BY ORION’S MAIN ENGINE'

verifications.claim: Orion's main engine is via the European Service Module.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'European Service Module, which provides... propulsion'; R5: 'ESM's AJ10 main engine'

verifications.claim: Firing of Orion's main engine puts the spacecraft on a trajectory toward the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Orion will fire its engines to push it on a path toward the moon'; R7: 'Lunar free return trajectory initiated'
verifications.reasoning: TLI burn sends to Moon trajectory.

verifications.claim: The spacecraft will fly to the far side of the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'passing over the far side'; R5: 'looping around the far side'; R7: 'lunar far side flyby'

verifications.claim: The spacecraft will fly roughly 3,000 to 9,000 miles above the Moon's surface.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'fly by the lunar far side at around 3,000-9,000 miles'; R1: 'about 4,000 miles above the surface'; R5: '4,067 mi'
verifications.reasoning: R4 matches range exactly; others within range.

verifications.claim: The spacecraft will use the Moon’s gravity to slingshot back toward Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'uses the moon’s gravity to swing the capsule directly back to Earth'; R5: 'free-return trajectory... slingshot'

verifications.claim: The spacecraft will not enter orbit around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'around the moon but not land there'; R5: 'lunar flyby mission... without entering lunar orbit'; R3: 'fly around our natural satellite'

verifications.claim: The return trip will take four days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'It will take around four days to make the journey back'; R7: 'travel time approximately 4 days'

verifications.claim: Re-entry speed will be over 25,000 mph.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R5: 're-entered Earth's atmosphere at a maximum velocity of about 24,664 miles per hour'
verifications.reasoning: Reference specifies 24,664 mph, which is under 25,000 mph.

verifications.claim: Splashdown will be in the Pacific Ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean'; R5: 'Pacific Ocean southwest of San Diego'

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is designed to test the crew systems in deep space.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'check that the spacecraft can safely make the journey and keep its crew alive'; R2: 'test the systems and hardware needed... in deep space'
verifications.reasoning: Primary goal is deep space crew systems test.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission will take the crew farther from Earth than any previous human mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'set a distance record... 252,799 miles, or 4,144 miles farther than the Apollo 13'; R5: 'set the record for human distance from Earth, 252,756 miles... breaking Apollo 13's record'
